_why: Eleven review rounds tried to decide, from the text of a shell script and a YAML workflow, whether the migration router is actually invoked. Parsing never finished; executing under stubs was neither faithful nor sealed; certifying a canonical line still left the container able to change its meaning (an array assignment, an escaped quote, a folded YAML scalar). This file ends the argument: the three call sites are FINGERPRINTED, and the guard compares bytes. Any edit to a call site fails `pnpm migration:route:controls` until a human re-records it here, which is what 'certified' has to mean when the alternative is a shell parser.
_how_to_update: Change the call site, then run `pnpm migration:route:controls --record` and review the diff to this file in the same commit as the change. Re-recording is a deliberate act; a reviewer seeing this file move should ask what moved with it.

.husky/pre-push.certifies: step 7 runs `printf '%s\n' "$PUSH_REFS" | corepack pnpm exec tsx scripts/migration-route.ts --run || exit 1` unconditionally at top level, which is the only runner the push-tier suites have

.github/workflows/ci.yml.certifies: the `migration` job runs `pnpm run migration:all` in an unconditional step, and `migration-controls` runs `pnpm run migration:controls` in its own job

_named_in_ci_why: Suites a ci.yml step names directly. Certified by the workflow fingerprint above, not by scanning the YAML: reading a `run:` payload out of its mapping is the inference this file exists to retire.
